svg.title: Point Forecasts vs Density Forecasts
svg.desc: A point forecast is about getting one mean right; a density forecast is about getting the whole distribution right. Risk questions are answered in the tail.
svg.text: Scoring a single number vs scoring an entire distribution
Only after the fact, via forecast errors
VaR and ES are read off directly
Check whether the PIT is uniform
The forecast comes out as one point
How wrong it could be is nowhere in the output
The forecast comes out as a whole distribution
Tail probabilities and quantiles can be read off directly
Square the errors and take the mean
Square, average → RMSE, a single number
Sign and shape vanish; only magnitude remains
The distribution is validated by whether the PIT is uniform
A U-shape means intervals too narrow; a hump, too wide
A point forecast gets one mean right; a density forecast gets the whole distribution right.
The moment risk matters, the answer lives in the tail — a question a point forecast cannot address.
Stationarity → memory → volatility → multivariate → evaluation closes the loop.
